title: Federal public servants’ wage-adjustment demonstration at the Central Bank
location: In front of the Central Bank of Brazil, Brasília, Federal District
scope: One reported morning gathering at the Central Bank; not a count for the broader multi-site federal workers’ action.
organizer: Federal public-service categories and organizations; exact on-site convenor not established in the body reviewed.
participants_original: UOL reports about 300 at the Central Bank citing the Banco Central estimate; Poder360 search-result excerpt reports about 250 there, attributed to organizers.
participants_precision: Two separately attributed approximate estimates for the same site; this is a reported range, not a statistical interval.
threshold_50_evidence: UOL’s article body reports about 300 at the Central Bank by the institution’s estimate; a Poder360 search-result excerpt gives about 250 at the same site. Both qualitative approximations clearly exceed 50; they are retained separately and not averaged or added to counts from other sites.

start_date.summary: UOL body and Poder360 search-result header place the Central Bank gathering on 18 January 2022.

end_date.summary: The reviewed UOL body does not give the Central Bank gathering’s end time/date; unknown.

location.summary: Both reports identify a gathering at/in front of the Central Bank in Brasília.

scope.summary: Reports describe a wider federal-worker action across sites; UOL confirms a Central Bank gathering and says an afternoon Ministry of Economy action was scheduled, not confirmed.

organizer.summary: Reports identify multiple federal public-service categories and organizations; exact local organizer is not resolved.

demands.summary: Federal workers sought salary adjustment/recomposition; UOL gives category-dependent figures of 20–28 percent.

participants_original.summary: UOL attributes about 300 to the Central Bank; Poder360 search-result excerpt reports about 250 attributed to organizers.

participants_min.summary: The low and high values are the two approximate reported counts; they are not bounds on the actual crowd.

participants_max.summary: The high value is the other approximate reported count; it is not a bound on the actual crowd.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both attributable estimates place the site-specific crowd well above 50.

state_target.summary: Salary recomposition from the federal employer/government was the stated demand.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed report does not describe violence by demonstrators; absence is not established, so unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No response to this gathering is established in the reviewed body; unknown.

state_response.arrests.summary: No arrest report in the reviewed body; unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: No beating evidence in the reviewed body; unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No dispersal attempt is reported in the reviewed body; unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The source does not establish whether the government ignored the gathering; unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: No deaths attributed to state forces are reported; unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: No shooting evidence is reported; unknown.

notes: A confirmed site-specific public gathering with reported turnout above 50 and a federal wage-policy demand. Do not transfer the Central Bank count to the planned Ministry of Economy action or to other cities. The broader action’s local/national episode boundaries remain for coordinator review.
open_questions: Whether simultaneous federal-worker acts at different sites form one national episode or separate local gatherings under the original codebook.
Exact end time and state responses at the Central Bank site remain unknown.

title: Protest against the proposed SuperVia rail-fare increase at Central do Brasil
location: Central do Brasil, central Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro state
scope: One local protest against the scheduled SuperVia passenger-fare increase. The regulator’s legal text establishes a state-authorized fare ceiling; the reports do not say that protesters named AGETRANSP as their addressee.
organizer: Movimento Contra o Aumento da Passagem, according to A Verdade; other participating groups are listed by that report.
participants_precision: Two qualitative reports; no numerical count or derived bounds.
threshold_50_evidence: Both reports describe hundreds at the same Central do Brasil protest, a qualitative count clearly above 50; no point estimate is inferred.

start_date.summary: Both reports date the protest to 25 January 2022.

end_date.summary: Repórter Popular gives 15:00–19:00 for this gathering; the record stores the date, not an unsupported hour-level field.

location.summary: Both reports place the demonstration at Central do Brasil in central Rio.

scope.summary: The reports describe a local rail-fare protest. The legal reproduction documents the state regulator’s fare authorization relevant to the protested increase.

organizer.summary: A Verdade identifies Movimento Contra o Aumento da Passagem as the organizing call and lists participating groups.

demands.summary: Reports describe opposition to the increase from R$5 to up to R$7. AGETRANSP’s reproduced act sets the authorized fare ceiling.

state_target.summary: The protest opposed the fare rise; LegisWeb reproduces AGETRANSP/CD Deliberação 1.223/21 authorizing up to R$7 from 2 February. The source is dependent legal-text evidence, not a written origin link or independent corroboration; reports do not show protesters naming the regulator.

participants_original.summary: Both local reports use qualitative “hundreds” descriptions.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both estimates are qualitative but clearly exceed 50; no exact number is derived.

protester_violence.summary: The sources do not establish violence by demonstrators; unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No state accommodation is described; unknown.

state_response.arrests.summary: No arrest evidence is described; unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: Repression is alleged in A Verdade, and Repórter Popular describes riders facing repression; neither read scope establishes a beating of protesters. Unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: A Verdade attributes the exact phrase “gás de borracha” to a report of shock-force repression; Repórter Popular reports cordons and closed station access. The sources do not clearly establish that this was an attempt to disperse the demonstration. Preserve the phrase without interpreting it as gunfire or a specific projectile; unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The sources do not establish whether the government ignored the protest; unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: No killing is reported in relation to this protest; unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: The phrase “gás de borracha” is not coded as shooting; no shooting evidence is established, so unknown.

fare_effective_at_event.summary: Official AGETRANSP search excerpts say the authorized R$7 fare was not practiced and R$5 continued under the 11th addendum; official body URLs were blocked/not found. Do not say R$7 was already being charged on 25 January.

notes: The state-policy connection is established through the reproduced state regulator act, while protest accounts frame the target as the fare increase and do not name AGETRANSP. The legal source says the new maximum took effect on 2 February; AGETRANSP search excerpts say R$7 was not practiced and R$5 continued. Service suspension/restart is not used as protest end. A Verdade’s “gás de borracha” is retained verbatim as attributed terminology only.
open_questions: Whether coordinator considers a protest against the fare increase sufficient evidence of a state-policy target when contemporary reports do not name AGETRANSP.
Whether the reported police entry/cordons/access closure constituted a dispersal attempt; no beating, shooting, arrest or death is established.
Official gazette/legal-source original URL is not supplied by LegisWeb; exact official body routes were unavailable as recorded.

title: Municipal doctors’ protest outside São Paulo City Hall
location: Outside São Paulo City Hall, São Paulo, São Paulo state
scope: Reported city-level doctors’ demonstration, distinct from the separately planned strike that a court enjoined.
organizer: Municipal primary-care doctors; a specific protest convenor is not confirmed in any opened source.
participants_original: CUT search-result excerpt reports about 100 doctors; body not available. Viomundo result mentions the Jan. 19 demonstration but gives no count.
participants_precision: One union-aligned search-result estimate; not independently verified.
threshold_50_evidence: The only numeric estimate is CUT’s search-result snippet (about 100); because the source body was not obtained, attendance remains unverified and eligibility is pending evidence.

start_date.summary: Retrospective CUT and Viomundo search-result excerpts report a Jan. 19 protest; advance reports said the protest was planned while the strike was separately enjoined.

end_date.summary: No search-result excerpt establishes the protest’s end; unknown.

location.summary: The search-result excerpts place the protest outside City Hall.

scope.summary: The planned labor stoppage and the City Hall protest were described separately; the strike was enjoined/suspended.

organizer.summary: Advance reports associate the labor action with medical unions; event organizer not confirmed in an opened body.

demands.summary: Search-result excerpts mention hiring doctors and improved work conditions; exact demand set is pending body verification.

state_target.summary: The reported hiring demand was directed at the municipal government/mayor; all cited material remains search-only.

participants_original.summary: CUT’s search-result excerpt reports approximately 100 doctors; no article body or independent estimate was obtained.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported approximately 100 would exceed 50 if confirmed; do not treat this search-result-only estimate as established.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Search-result summaries mention court/employer developments but do not establish state accommodation to the protest; unknown.

notes: This remains a provisional lead because attendance and event details are available only in search-result excerpts. Do not treat the struck-down strike as the public gathering or treat the injunction as proof of protest dispersal.
open_questions: Obtain accessible body evidence or a contemporaneous independent account of occurrence and turnout.
Confirm exact organizer, demands, event end and state responses from article text.
